history.wave 1/2 (ws-B, CORE-POP c5c/w2-corepop): columnar population, profiles, event-driven activation, popweb over net.fetch, purchases through the bank, class 2 adaptive groups, a 4-head class 3, package API of ONE_WORLD_CONTRACTS section 1, gate tests B/G/SP-3.x/SP-4.1 (no report: the wave-2 engineer was stopped before writing one)
history.wave 3b (this branch): fitted runtime models in class 1 (D-30), provenance on every population batch, class 3 redesign (D-31), class 2 activity choice and memory through time (D-32), SP-3.2c/SP-4.0/SP-4.4 gate tests, criteria asserted in every B-owned gate test

limitations: session_minutes@1 is not used: its minutes count KuaiRand pool videos only (median 0.06-0.2 min per session) and its contract declares no scale factor; session length stays the individual's plausible log-normal (pop.decision.session_length).

daily_return@1 has no content, notification or satisfaction inputs: the population's daily activity does not respond to what platforms show (satisfaction acts through activity choice, abandonment and returns to resources).
extra_sessions@1 is served as the E3 review's constant C2 rate (no individual heterogeneity in sessions per active day).

article_open_semantic@1 is a news-article model (MIND) extrapolated to the population's web page slates; its text affinity is the cosine of the individual's interests (which drift towards consumed items) with the headline, not the mean embedding of its consumed items; own topic views are tracked for the four most read topics.
customer_return@1 gives P(another order within 90 days); the day of that order is drawn from the customer's own mean gap (30 days after a first order).
Generated web sites (popsites) still write their articles from the 16-topic lexicon templates; strategic participants and population members write from the real corpus (population.writing).
Class 3 roles are entrepreneurs/publishers, competitors and collaborators; researchers, engineers, employees, organisations and investors are not class-3 roles here.

Personal memory benefit in the integrated worlds is measured (SP-3.4) but small by construction: most of what predicts an individual's utility is in its observation; the BPTT unit test shows the memory can carry hidden traits.

Population worlds with sandboxed sites are not reproducible across worlds in one process (DEF-P-27, D-20 metering memo: cloud.usage cpu_ms differs); tests/test_v5_population_core.py::test_same_seed_same_hashes_replay_regeneration_and_resume fails at the integration head for that reason (first divergence: cloud.usage of a page fetch).
integration_notes: E (calibration): register the population's in-world probes: `from crucible.population import fidelity_probes; INWORLD_PROBES.update(fidelity_probes.PROBES)` (lazy, inside inworld_claims) - the register's default claims population.daily_return / session_frequency / article_choice and commerce.customer_retention need them (population code may import only calibration.runtime).

E (calibration): two tests of tests/test_v5_calibration_inworld.py assume the population records no fitted decision of its own, which is no longer true (D-30): test_wired_world_decisions_count_and_agree_with_check_provenance asserts that pop.session/pop.activation carry no provenance (replace by `assert m['decision_events_without_model_provenance'] == 0`; pop.activation is merged into pop.session), and test_stamped_decisions_without_runtime_evaluation_do_not_count asserts fitted_models_used_in_world == 0 in a world whose population now takes daily_return@1 / extra_sessions@1 decisions (check instead that no counted batch has kind calibstamp.*, i.e. the stamped batches are unbacked).
E (calibration): session_minutes@1 needs a declared scale factor (share of app time its pool-video minutes stand for) before a population can use it for session length.

C (social): the feed's sessions should spend at most `population.session_budget(world, idx)` minutes (the population's session length); population.activation counts items reached from minutes when an activity does not report them (pop.tick.items).

C (social): SP-4.0 needs the population's own activity on every Part 4 platform (short/long video, images, messaging, creator subscriptions, newsletters, developer and knowledge platforms); population.analysis.platform_activity counts impress./consume. decision batches, relation-table decisions and member events per platform.

D (semantic): pop_semantic binds class 4 through population.register_class_runtime; the binding contract is documented there (rows, activation, session provenance model class4.<owner>, attention, experience). SP-3.2 composes pop_semantic into its world when the module is registered.
O / orchestrator: DEF-P-27 (D-20 metering memo) breaks same-process determinism of population worlds with sandboxed sites.

M (perf): population hot paths changed - forum feeds shared by readers with the same follow set, post representations cached per text, article slates assembled once per page, web/purchase columns declared only by popweb (internet profile rows ~0.6 KB lighter).

M (perf): scale/gatev.py's dense policy observer evaluates pop.models['session_start'] if present; that decision is retired (D-30) - the population's activation policy is now runtime daily_return@1 / extra_sessions@1 (population.activation.decide_day), which the dense arm should evaluate for every eligible individual instead.
